It exits early if price returns to the previous close, the stop sits half the opening move beyond the signal close, and CPI and payroll mornings are skipped.

The mechanism is liquidity provision: market makers absorb the burst of opening orders that follow a big over

I wrote the proposal to `research/proxies/proposals/P-009.json`. The rule trades US500 only, in the last hour of the last three sessions of each month. It goes against the month-to-date move when that move is at least 0.5%, and it skips FOMC days.

**Mechanism:** pensions and balanced funds rebalance to fixed stock/bond weights at month-end. They must sell equities after an up month and buy after a down month, in large, predictable, price-insensitive orders that go mostly through the close. The rule takes the other side alongside the liquidity providers who are paid to absorb that flow.

I wrote the proposal to `research/proxies/proposals/P-011.json`. It is a round-number rejection fade on US500 only.

**Mechanism:** take-profit and resting limit orders pile up at round numbers (here, multiples of 50 S&P points). On the first touch of the day they form a wall that turns the price. The rule fades a bar that tests such a level and fails to close through it. Its stop sits 0.15% beyond the level, past the stop-loss cluster that sits just beyond it.
